questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Opposite directions

options.explanation: Correct. The opposite of a direction is found by flipping both letters: North becomes South and East becomes West, so NE becomes SW.
Only the East part was flipped to West; the North was left unchanged. A true opposite flips both letters.
Only the North part was flipped to South. This is a quarter turn away, not the opposite.

options.explanation: 90 degrees clockwise from North reaches East, not South-East. South-East is one further ordinal step.
Correct. Each compass point is 45 degrees apart. North to South-East clockwise is three steps: North, North-East, East, South-East, that is 3 × 45 = 135 degrees.
45 degrees clockwise from North reaches North-East, only one step. South-East is three steps away.

questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Single-turn distance
questions.stem: Sunil walks 4 km towards the East, then turns left and walks 3 km. How far is he from his starting point?

options.explanation: 7 km is the total distance walked, 4 + 3. The question asks for the straight-line distance from the start, which is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
This subtracts the legs, 4 − 3. The two legs are perpendicular, so they combine by Pythagoras, not by subtraction.
Correct. Facing East then turning left faces North, so the finish is 4 East and 3 North. Distance = √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 km.

options.explanation: 2 km subtracts the distances, 8 − 6. That is right only when both run the same way; here they run opposite ways, so the gap is the sum.
Correct. They run in opposite directions from one point, so the gap is the sum: 6 + 8 = 14 km.
10 km would arise from a right triangle, but North and South are along one line, so the moves add straight, not by Pythagoras.
This is the product 6 × 8, not a distance.

questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Direction of one walker from another
questions.stem: P and Q start from the same spot. P walks towards the East and Q walks towards the West. In which direction is Q from P?

options.explanation: East is the direction P walked. Q went the opposite way, so Q is on the West side of P.
Correct. P moves East and Q moves West from the same start, so Q ends up to the West of P.
Neither walker moved North or South, so the direction between them is along the East–West line.
Neither walker moved North or South, so the direction between them is along the East–West line.

questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Relative direction chain
questions.stem: A is to the East of B. B is to the North of C. In which direction is C from A?

options.explanation: C is south and west of A, so it lies in the South-West quadrant, not the North-East.
Correct. Place B at the centre: A is East of B, and C is South of B. From A, then, C is both to the West and to the South, that is South-West.
C is to the West of A, not the East, because A lies East of B while C sits below B.
C is to the South of A, not the North, because C is below B while A is level with B.

questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Mirror reflection
questions.stem: A man walks towards the North and sees his reflection approaching in a plane mirror straight ahead. In which direction does the reflection appear to move?

options.explanation: The reflection moves towards him, opposite to his own motion, so it cannot move North with him.
Correct. A plane mirror facing him reverses the direction crossing it, so as he walks North his reflection appears to walk South towards him.
The reflection moves along the same line he walks, North–South, reversed. It does not move sideways.

The market is West of the school, not East, because the school lies East of the library while the market is below the library.
Correct. Put the library at the centre: the school is East of it and the market is South of it. From the school, the market is both West and South, that is South-West.

questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Negative marking judgement
questions.stem: Paper 3 deducts 0.25 mark for each wrong answer and gives 1 mark for each correct one. Which is the best guidance for a direction-sense question you are unsure of?

options.text: Never attempt any question, to avoid the penalty
options.explanation: This forgoes marks you could reasonably win. Direction questions are checkable by redrawing, so many can be answered with confidence.

options.text: Attempt when you can eliminate at least one option, since the drawing is checkable
options.explanation: Correct. Eliminating even one option makes the expected value of a guess clearly positive, and a redrawn path usually confirms the answer, so attempting is worthwhile.

options.text: Always guess blindly, because there is no penalty
options.explanation: There is a penalty of 0.25 for a wrong answer, so blind guessing is only marginally positive and carries wide risk.

options.text: Attempt only if you are 100% certain, otherwise always leave it
options.explanation: This is too cautious. Once one or two options are eliminated, an attempt is clearly worth making even without full certainty.

questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Longer walk to a triple
questions.stem: A surveyor walks 26 m North, 10 m East, 2 m South and 3 m West. How far is she from her starting point?

options.explanation: 41 m is the total walked, 26 + 10 + 2 + 3, not the straight-line distance.
Correct. Net North = 26 − 2 = 24, net East = 10 − 3 = 7, so distance = √(7² + 24²) = √625 = 25 m, the 7-24-25 triple.
33 m uses 26 and 7 without cancelling the South leg. Reduce each axis first: North becomes 24, East becomes 7.
17 m subtracts the net gaps, 24 − 7. Perpendicular gaps combine by Pythagoras.

questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Turns forming a spiral
questions.stem: Facing East, a drone flies 15 m, turns left and flies 13 m, turns left and flies 3 m, turns left and flies 8 m. How far is it from the launch point?

options.explanation: 39 m is the total flown, 15 + 13 + 3 + 8, not the straight-line distance.
Correct. Tracking the heading: East 15, then North 13, then West 3, then South 8. Net East = 15 − 3 = 12, net North = 13 − 8 = 5, so distance = √(12² + 5²) = √169 = 13 m.
17 m adds the net gaps, 12 + 5. Perpendicular gaps combine by Pythagoras, giving 13 m.
7 m subtracts the net gaps, 12 − 5. The gaps combine by Pythagoras, not by subtraction.

questions.topic: Ch 10 · Direction Sense · Distance and direction together
questions.stem: From his hostel, Vikram walks 5 m East, 15 m North, 4 m East and 3 m South. How far is he from the hostel, and in which direction?

options.explanation: The direction is right, but 21 m is close to the total walked, not the straight-line distance. That distance is 15 m.
Correct. Net East = 5 + 4 = 9, net North = 15 − 3 = 12, so distance = √(9² + 12²) = √225 = 15 m, and being up and to the right the finish lies North-East of the hostel.
The distance is right, but South-West is the direction of the hostel from Vikram, not of Vikram from the hostel. He is North-East of the hostel.
3 m subtracts the net gaps, 12 − 9. The perpendicular gaps combine by Pythagoras to give 15 m.
